assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and molecular sieves with controlled pore architecture and active sites is a clear case of structure determining function, with huge industrial reach in refining, emissions control and fine chemicals. As a structural chemist I value that these designs were verified by actual crystal structures and not only by activity data.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalyst design and active-site engineering), Davis (synthesis of new framework types, chiral and extra-large-pore materials) and Zones (structure-directing agents, SSZ materials, Chevron's CHA catalysts) are decisive contributors. Credit is spread across many groups, so a three-person split is defensible but not unique; Yu and Tsapatsis also have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and deployed technology; recognition is not premature. The risk is the opposite: the field is broad and the committee may see it as diffuse.
uncertainties: The exact discovery to honour (new frameworks, SDA design or catalyst engineering) is not sharply defined.
Whether industrial credit (Zones) will weigh as heavily as academic credit is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites as solution-processable absorbers moved from a few percent to over 25 percent efficiency in little over a decade, an unusually rapid and far-reaching change in energy materials with crystal-structure and defect chemistry at its core.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park the solid-state ~9 percent device, Snaith the efficiency leaps and thin-film perovskite design. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel are also strong, so the credit is contested beyond three seats.
assessment.maturity: Impact and independent reproduction are overwhelming, but long-term operational stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, which argues that the field is not yet fully mature.
uncertainties: Device lifetime and commercial viability are not settled.
Which three of six or more credible names is disputed; my knowledge of the early priority history is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation via PROTACs and molecular glues opens a new pharmacological modality: chemistry that rewires the ubiquitin system. Several degraders are in clinical trials, and structure-based ternary-complex design is central to the mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli provided structural and VHL-ligand design that made them drug-like. The thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue discovery (Handa, Ito) is a separate thread that complicates a three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Strong mechanistic and structural confirmation; clinical validation is still maturing, so timing is slightly early but plausible.
uncertainties: No degrader has yet shown broad approved-drug impact.
The PROTAC and molecular-glue histories may need separate recognition and the committee may disagree on how to split credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes created a large new family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides with tunable composition and surface terminations. It is a genuine materials-chemistry discovery with broad applications in energy storage, EMI shielding and sensing, and the structural characterization is well documented.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Ti3C2 discovery by Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum is clearly attributed, with the MAX-phase background from Barsoum. The three-person configuration is natural and unusually clean.
assessment.maturity: Rapid growth and many independent groups; applications are still emerging, so a modest degree of prematurity remains.
uncertainties: Real-world device impact is still limited.
Terminations and structure in real samples are heterogeneous, which weakens some structural claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from nano- and microcrystals and time-resolved studies of reactions, extending crystallography to what conventional sources cannot reach. This is an enabling method of the type I value.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof of concept and methodology; Fromme (photosystem I nanocrystals) and Schlichting (time-resolved work) are prominent. Hajdu's role in the original concept is important, and I am not certain of his current status; this complicates a fair three-person split.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely adopted at multiple facilities, but access is limited and chemistry impact is narrower than for synchrotron methods.
uncertainties: Facility scarcity limits breadth of impact.
Credit between concept, methods and applications is contested, and Hajdu's eligibility is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-atom catalysts push heterogeneous catalysis to maximum atom efficiency with defined active sites, a concept now explored in thousands of studies and linked to atomic-resolution microscopy and spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Pt1/FeOx work of Qiao, Wang, Zhang and coworkers, and Liu's earlier electron-microscopy work on isolated atoms, form the main lines. Earlier precedents in the literature complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: A young field with problems of stability at realistic loadings and of proof that single atoms rather than clusters are the active species; recognition may be early.
uncertainties: Some claims rely on characterization where cluster contributions are hard to exclude.
Priority relative to earlier isolated-atom studies is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ordered mesoporous silica (MCM-41, SBA-15, and later ordered carbons) established surfactant-templated assembly of tunable mesopores, a core framework-materials concept that influenced catalysis, separation and nanostructure design. I note a field-related bias here, and I weigh it against the modest commercial and functional follow-through.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck (Mobil) discovered MCM-41, Stucky (SBA-15, general templating) and Ryoo (ordered mesoporous carbons, MCM-48 mechanism and zeolite nanosheets) drove the broader chemistry; Inagaki's FSM-16 is an important independent precedent. The attribution is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with thirty years of confirmation; the peak of discovery excitement has passed, which may weigh on timing.
uncertainties: Real industrial impact has been less than anticipated.
Priority between FSM-16 (Inagaki) and MCM-41 complicates the configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a workhorse transformation in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, a clear case of a catalyst design having a very large practical impact. The mechanistic understanding is well developed.
assessment.attribution: Kosugi reported the early tin-amide coupling; Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general amine coupling and ligands. The attribution is reasonably clean, although the 2010 Nobel Prize in cross-coupling covers related chemistry.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and broadly validated. The weakness is overlap with the 2010 prize rather than immaturity.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Kosugi's precise contribution relative to the others is from memory.
